beat1: It's 2 a.m. An AI tells someone why they can't sleep.
beat2: Now Jamie Zeitzer's name is on the answer.

beat3.headline: Backed by his team at the Stanford School of Medicine.
beat3.body1: Prof. Jamie Zeitzer co-directs the Stanford Center for Sleep and Circadian Sciences. Every answer your users see is grounded in the corpus he and his team have published — and refuses when it isn't.
beat3.body2: This is Science, signed — governed, scientist-signed expert knowledge for agents, not a generic answers API.

integration.headline: From "interesting" to a working POST in five minutes.
integration.body: Hand this page to your engineering team. One endpoint, streaming Server-Sent Events, structured Stanford-grounded output. The full interactive reference (live request console, response shape, structured-answer format) lives at
integration.curlHint: Five lines. Streams Server-Sent Events back. Each
integration.curlHint2: line is a JSON object — concatenate
integration.curlHint3: deltas to assemble the structured answer.
integration.authBody1: Every pilot gets a private partner key, scoped to their domain and usage tier. Send it as the
integration.authBody2: header on every request. Keys are issued by email after a short pilot conversation — there's no signup form yet on purpose, because each pilot has different attribution and refusal needs that we want to tune up front.
integration.authBody3: To request a key, use the partners channel from the homepage CTA with your product name, the surface where answers will appear, and an estimate of monthly question volume.
integration.authHint: During the open pilot window the endpoint also accepts unauthenticated requests for evaluation. Production traffic must use a key.
integration.rateHint3: header (seconds). Implement exponential backoff starting at 1s; treat any 5xx the same way.

integration.versionBreakingBody: v1 stays online for at least 6 months after v2 launches; pilots get 30 days' advance notice by email.

integration.chatgptBody: For Custom GPTs, Claude tools, and any agent that just wants one structured JSON object back (not a token stream), there's a synchronous companion endpoint with a published OpenAPI 3.0 spec. Paste the spec URL into your tool's import field — no SDK required.

guarantee.headline: When the research doesn't cover it, the answer says so.
guarantee.body: Every answer Palonur returns is either grounded in the Zeitzer corpus or explicitly refused — with a clean
guarantee.body2: prefix your parser can branch on. No hallucinated citations. No confident guesses. A named scientist's refusal is the product, not a failure mode.

closing.headline: Ready to ship Stanford sleep science?
closing.body: Every pilot starts with a short conversation about your use case — the surface, the volume, the attribution model. That's it.
